data.narrative:
Zeromark is a Seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Joel Anderson that has raised $10M+. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 10 comparable companies: 2 public entities (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic, spanning Seed through Series A stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-Progression analysis uses Zeromark's $10M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $25M. Peer-Median analysis across 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Stark Defence ($4.0B Series A), UFORCE ($1.0B Seed), Singularity ($400M Series A), and NODA AI ($125M Series A)—produces a median of $700M, with a range of $125M to $4.0B.

The triangulated valuation range is $21M (low) to $805M (high), with a median of $362M. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in the peer-comparable approach, driven by outsized valuations at the Series A stage and a single Seed-stage comparable (UFORCE) at $1.0B. The Stage-Progression method grounds the low end but assumes typical step-up multiples without product-market validation data. Critical unknowns include Zeromark's revenue trajectory, product differentiation relative to the peer set, and customer traction in a sector where government procurement patterns drive valuation materiality.
